questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.My colour TV, ______ I bought 10 years ago, still gives beautiful pictures.

options.explain: correct -- non-restrictive relative pronoun for a thing
"that" can't introduce a non-restrictive clause after a comma
not a valid relative pronoun here
would leave the clause without a needed relative pronoun after a comma

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.He is very stubborn, so it will be difficult to ______ him to go.

options.explain: correct -- "persuade someone to do something" fits "stubborn"
wrong structure -- doesn't take object + to-infinitive
would need a bare infinitive, not "to go"
wrong meaning -- opposite of getting him to go

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence."Who is Mr. Madely?" "I have no idea. I've never heard ______ him".

options.explain: wrong preposition for this fixed phrase
wrong preposition -- "hear from" means to receive a message
correct -- "never heard of someone" means not knowing they exist

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.Children are ______ to overcome problems.

options.explain: bare verb, wrong word class after "are"
wrong word -- means a deciding factor

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.They will be sent to work in America ______ their English is better next year.

options.explain: wrong meaning -- doesn't express a condition
wrong meaning -- would reverse the intended condition
correct -- introduces the condition for being sent
wrong meaning -- doesn't fit a future condition

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.I've never ______ very well with my brother. We've got completely different personalities.

options.explain: correct -- "get on with someone" means to have a good relationship

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.______ lion dancing is very popular in Viet Nam, my friend, Andy does not enjoy it.

options.explain: can't join two clauses this way
correct -- shows contrast between popularity and Andy not enjoying it
can't join two clauses this way

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.I believe that our new manager has the ______ to work well in this business environment.

options.explain: wrong word class, and wrong meaning

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.When my father retired, he decided to take ______ golf.

options.explain: correct -- "take up a hobby" is the fixed phrasal verb

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option (A, B, C or D) to complete each sentence.That's a nice coat, and the colour ______ you well.

options.explain: wrong verb -- "match" compares two things to each other
correct -- "a colour suits someone" describes it looking good on them

Read the passage. Write T (True) if the statement is true, F (False) if it is false, or N (No information) if the passage doesn't say.A language everyone knows

There is one language we all speak, no matter what country we live in: The language of numbers.

The language of numbers is called mathematics. You are learning it in school now. The simplest kind is called arithmetic. In high school and college you'll learn other kinds of mathematics. To help all of us with mathematics, machines have been invented. They let us do problems faster and with fewer mistakes. We know that the abacus or counting board was the first of these machines. It was invented many thousands of years ago, but it is still used in China, Japan and other countries. Today, computers are used all over the world. These computers seem to think. Of course, they really don't. They do only what people tell them to do. But they do it much better and faster than a person could. Inside, a computer may look very confusing to you. But the people who run it know just what to do. They can make a computer store up facts and give them to other people. They can make it solve hard problems and help us to live better. Like people all over the world, these machines speak the same language: numbers.The simplest kind of mathematics is Arithmetic.
